question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

YZ, WX, UU, ?, QL, OF, MY, KQ
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. SQ.

GIVEN

• YZ, WX, UU, ?, QL, OF, MY, KQ

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: Y(25), W(23), U(21), ?, Q(17), O(15), M(13), K(11) → constant −2, so missing = 19 = S.

• 2nd letters: Z(26), X(24), U(21), ?, L(12), F(6), Y(25), Q(17) → gaps −2, −3, −4, −5, −6, −7, −8; the 4th gap is −5 from Q, i.e. U(21)−4 = Q(17).

• So the missing term = SQ.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• First letters drop by 2 (fixed); second letters drop by an increasing count (−2,−3,−4…). Fix first letter = S, then just fill the widening second-letter gap → Q.

NOTE

• In two-letter series always split into the two columns and check each column's own rule (A=1 … Z=26). One column is usually constant, the other progressive.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

? , IJ, GE, EY, CR, AJ, YA, WQ
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. KN.

GIVEN

• ?, IJ, GE, EY, CR, AJ, YA, WQ

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: ?, I(9), G(7), E(5), C(3), A(1), Y(25), W(23) → constant −2, so before I(9) comes 11 = K.

• 2nd letters: ?, J(10), E(5), Y(25), R(18), J(10), A(1), Q(17) → gaps −5, −6, −7, −8, −9, −10 (mod 26); the first gap (term1→term2) is −4, so 2nd letter = J(10)+4 = 14 = N.

• So the missing term = KN.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• First column −2 fixed → K. Second column drops by growing steps ending in J; step back one more (−4) to get N.

NOTE

• When a letter goes below A, wrap: subtract using mod 26 (e.g. E−6 = −1 ≡ 25 = Y).

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter cluster in the same way as the first letter cluster is related to the second letter cluster and fifth letter cluster is related to sixth letter cluster.

RS : OH :: ? : VV :: TM : QN
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. YE.

GIVEN

• RS : OH :: ? : VV :: TM : QN

SOLUTION

• Rule (from the known pairs): 1st letter −3; 2nd letter → its opposite (mirror) letter (A↔Z, i.e. sum 27).

• Check: RS→OH: R−3=O, S(19)→opposite = 8 = H ✓. TM→QN: T−3=Q, M(13)→opposite = 14 = N ✓.

• Apply to fourth cluster VV: 1st letter V(22)+3 = 25 = Y; 2nd letter V(22)→opposite = 5 = E.

• So ? = YE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• First letters differ by a fixed 3; the second letter is just the mirror image (A↔Z). Reverse both to jump from VV back to YE.

NOTE

• Opposite/mirror letter: position + mirror = 27 (A↔Z, B↔Y, S↔H, E↔V). Memorise the EJOTY pairs to do this instantly.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(FG, HI, LM)

(LK, NM, RQ)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. (KT, MV, QZ).

GIVEN

• (FG, HI, LM) and (LK, NM, RQ)

SOLUTION

• Rule: within a set the three clusters' 1st letters rise by +2, +4 (F,H,L / L,N,R) and the 2nd letters likewise by +2,+4; the gap between the two letters of each cluster is constant (FG,HI,LM = +1; LK,NM,RQ = −1).

• Option (KT, MV, QZ): 1st letters K,M,Q → +2,+4 ✓; 2nd letters T,V,Z → +2,+4 ✓; inner gap K→T, M→V, Q→Z = +9 constant ✓.

• Others fail: (RN,TO,WX) 1st letters R,T,W → +2,+3 ✗.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just check the three first-letters: they must step +2 then +4. Only KT, MV, QZ (K→M→Q) does that with a fixed inner gap.

NOTE

• In 'find the matching set' problems, first test the leading letters' pattern across clusters, then confirm the constant inner offset.

question: What will be the sum of number of Sundays in the month of October of 2009 and January of 2010?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 9.

GIVEN

• Sundays in October 2009 + Sundays in January 2010.

SOLUTION

• 1 Jan 2009 = Thursday; days up to 1 Oct = 273 ≡ 0 (mod 7), so 1 Oct 2009 = Thursday. Sundays fall on 4, 11, 18, 25 = 4 Sundays.

• 1 Oct→1 Jan 2010: Oct(31)+Nov(30)+Dec(31)=92 ≡ 1, so 1 Jan 2010 = Friday. Sundays on 3, 10, 17, 24, 31 = 5 Sundays.

• Sum = 4 + 5 = 9.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• A 31-day month has 5 of a weekday only if that day is the 1st, 2nd or 3rd. Oct starts Thu (Sun is 4th → 4), Jan starts Fri (Sun is 3rd → 5). 4+5=9.

NOTE

• Odd days: count days between dates, take mod 7. Thu=known anchor; add month lengths mod 7 to shift weekday.

question: Which of the following pairs of years have identical calendars?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1954 and 1965.

GIVEN

• Find the pair of years with identical calendars.

SOLUTION

• Calendars repeat when total odd days from the first year up to (but not including) the second year ≡ 0 (mod 7), with matching leap status.

• 1954→1965: years 1954…1964 = 11 years, leap years 1956, 1960, 1964 = 3. Odd days = 11 + 3 = 14 ≡ 0 (mod 7) ✓.

• 1954 is an ordinary year, so its calendar recurs in 1965.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• An ordinary year's calendar usually repeats after 6 or 11 years. 1954 (ordinary) + 11 = 1965; the 3 leaps in between make 11+3 = 14 = a clean 2 weeks.

NOTE

• Odd days per ordinary year = 1, per leap year = 2. Sum from start year to just before target must be a multiple of 7.

question: 5 teachers P, Q, R, S and T are sitting in a row facing south (not necessarily in the same order). P is third to the right of T. S is fourth to the right of T. Q is second to the right of T. Who is sitting to the immediate left of Q?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. R.

GIVEN

• Row faces south. P is 3rd right of T, S is 4th right of T, Q is 2nd right of T.

SOLUTION

• Facing south, a person's right = west. Take T as reference; count 'right' towards the west.

• Positions (west→east): S(4th right), P(3rd right), Q(2nd right), R, T. The only leftover person R takes the 1st-right seat.

• Arrangement: S, P, Q, R, T.

• Immediate left of Q (left = east side) = R.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Place T, put S/P/Q at their 'right' distances (4,3,2) on the same side; the gap of 1 is auto-filled by R, who sits just left of Q.

NOTE

• Facing south → right = west, left = east (mirror of facing north). Always fix the facing direction before reading left/right.

question: Marks of 6 girls P, Q, R, S, T and U are compared. Marks of no two girls are same. Marks of P are not less than anyone. Marks of U and R both are more than both S and T but less than Q. Marks of U and R are 300 and 400 respectively. Marks of how many girls are less than U?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2.

GIVEN

• P ≥ everyone (highest). U, R > S and > T but < Q. U = 300, R = 400.

SOLUTION

• Since R(400) > U(300) and both < Q, and P is the largest: P > Q > R(400) > U(300).

• S and T are both less than U and R, so S, T < 300.

• Ranking: P > Q > R > U > {S, T}.

• Girls with marks less than U = S and T = 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Only S and T sit below U in the chain; everyone else (P, Q, R) is above. So exactly 2 are less than U.

NOTE

• Convert each verbal comparison into one long inequality chain; then simply count names on the required side.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and fourth letter-number cluster is related to third letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

AK50 : CM78 :: TP70 : VR98 :: OQ60 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. QS88.

GIVEN

• AK50 : CM78 :: TP70 : VR98 :: OQ60 : ?

SOLUTION

• Rule (from the known pairs): each letter +2, number +28.

• Check: A+2=C, K+2=M, 50+28=78 ✓; T+2=V, P+2=R, 70+28=98 ✓.

• Apply to OQ60: O+2=Q, Q+2=S, 60+28=88 → QS88.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Shift both letters forward by 2 and add 28 to the number. O→Q, Q→S, 60→88.

NOTE

• Treat the number as a whole (no digit-splitting, as the note warns). Find the letter shift and the arithmetic step separately.

question:
Select the option that is related to the second letter-number cluster in the same way as the third letter-number cluster is related to the fourth letter-number cluster and fifth letter-number cluster is related to sixth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

? : TT75 :: ZA60 : WJ90 :: HH80 : EQ120
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. WK50.

GIVEN

• ? : TT75 :: ZA60 : WJ90 :: HH80 : EQ120

SOLUTION

• Rule (from known pairs): 1st letter −3, 2nd letter +9, number ×1.5.

• Check: Z−3=W, A+9=J, 60×1.5=90 ✓; H−3=E, H+9=Q, 80×1.5=120 ✓.

• We need ? → TT75. Reverse the rule: 1st letter = T+3 = W; 2nd letter = T−9 = K; number = 75÷1.5 = 50 → WK50.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Since ? maps TO TT75, undo the rule: +3 on 1st letter (T→W), −9 on 2nd (T→K), ÷1.5 on number (75→50).

NOTE

• When the unknown is on the left of the colon, invert every operation (−3 becomes +3, ×1.5 becomes ÷1.5).

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and fifth number is related to sixth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

7157 : 7192 :: ? : 4813 :: 68 : 103
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 4778.

GIVEN

• 7157 : 7192 :: ? : 4813 :: 68 : 103

SOLUTION

• Rule (from known pairs): second = first + 35.

• Check: 7157 + 35 = 7192 ✓; 68 + 35 = 103 ✓.

• So ? + 35 = 4813 → ? = 4813 − 35 = 4778.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The pattern is simply +35. As the unknown is the left term, subtract: 4813 − 35 = 4778.

NOTE

• Numbers are treated whole. First fix the constant difference from a clean pair (68→103), then apply it.

question:
Select the option that is related to the first number in the same way as the fourth number is related to the third number and sixth number is related to fifth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

802 : ? :: 1940 : 968 :: 1012 : 504
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 399.

GIVEN

• 802 : ? :: 1940 : 968 :: 1012 : 504

SOLUTION

• Rule (from known pairs): result = number ÷ 2 − 2.

• Check: 1940÷2 − 2 = 970 − 2 = 968 ✓; 1012÷2 − 2 = 506 − 2 = 504 ✓.

• So ? = 802÷2 − 2 = 401 − 2 = 399.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Halve the number, then knock off 2: 802 → 401 → 399.

NOTE

• Test a simple pair first (1012→504) to spot 'half minus 2'; then apply to the unknown.

question: In a certain coded language 'TREK' is coded as 'WVAF' and 'SIGN' is coded as 'VMCI'. How will 'SLAY' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. VPWT.

GIVEN

• TREK → WVAF ; SIGN → VMCI

SOLUTION

• Position-wise shifts: +3, +4, −4, −5.

• Check TREK: T+3=W, R+4=V, E−4=A, K−5=F ✓. SIGN: S+3=V, I+4=M, G−4=C, N−5=I ✓.

• SLAY: S+3=V, L+4=P, A−4=23=W, Y−5=T → VPWT.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Remember the shift pattern +3, +4, −4, −5 and apply letter by letter (wrap A−4 = W).

NOTE

• For coding, line the code under the word and read each column's shift; wrap with mod 26 when it crosses A or Z.

question: In a certain coded language 'TWEAK' is coded as 'UYHWF' and 'STATS' is coded as 'TVDPN'. How will 'FIVES' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. GKYAN.

GIVEN

• TWEAK → UYHWF ; STATS → TVDPN

SOLUTION

• Position-wise shifts: +1, +2, +3, −4, −5.

• Check TWEAK: T+1=U, W+2=Y, E+3=H, A−4=W, K−5=F ✓. STATS: S+1=T, T+2=V, A+3=D, T−4=P, S−5=N ✓.

• FIVES: F+1=G, I+2=K, V+3=Y, E−4=A, S−5=N → GKYAN.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Apply +1, +2, +3, −4, −5 across the 5 letters (A−4 wraps to W-style; here E−4=A).

NOTE

• Increasing-then-decreasing shifts are common; write positions (A=1…Z=26) and add/subtract, wrapping mod 26.

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

GM101, ZN155, RO210, LP263, EQ317, XR371
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. RO210.

GIVEN

• GM101, ZN155, RO210, LP263, EQ317, XR371

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: G(7), Z(26/0), ?, L(12), E(5), X(24) → step −7 (mod 26): G, Z, S, L, E, X. The 3rd should be S, not R.

• 2nd letters: M, N, O, P, Q, R → perfect +1 (all correct).

• Numbers: 101, 155, ?, 263, 317, 371 → constant +54: 101, 155, 209, 263, 317, 371. The 3rd should be 209, not 210.

• Both flags point to the 3rd term: it should be SO209, so the wrong term is RO210.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Numbers jump by a steady +54; 155+54 = 209, but the term shows 210 → that term (RO210) is the odd one.

NOTE

• For mixed letter-number series, check each part (1st letter, 2nd letter, number) as its own progression; a wrong term usually breaks one of them.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

RUC705, QTB819, PSA933, ?, NQY1161
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. ORZ1047.

GIVEN

• RUC705, QTB819, PSA933, ?, NQY1161

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: R, Q, P, ?, N → −1 each → O.

• 2nd letters: U, T, S, ?, Q → −1 each → R.

• 3rd letters: C, B, A, ?, Y → −1 each (A−1 wraps to Z) → Z.

• Numbers: 705, 819, 933, ?, 1161 → +114 each → 933 + 114 = 1047.

• So the missing term = ORZ1047.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Each letter steps back by 1 (A→Z wrap) and the number rises by 114. P→O, S→R, A→Z, 933→1047.

NOTE

• Split three-letter + number terms into 4 independent tracks; the number gap (here 114 = 819−705) locks the answer fast.

question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 9 AM and 10 AM will the hour and minute hands of the clock overlap?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 9:49.

GIVEN

• Hour and minute hands overlap between 9 AM and 10 AM.

SOLUTION

• Overlap past H o'clock occurs at (60H/11) minutes. For H = 9: 60×9/11 = 540/11 = 49.09 min.

• So the hands coincide at about 9:49 AM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Overlap minute = (60 × hour)/11. Here 540/11 ≈ 49 → 9:49.

NOTE

• The hands overlap 11 times every 12 hours, i.e. once every 65·5/11 min. Between H and H+1 the overlap is at (60H/11) minutes past H.

question: A clock was set right at 4 AM on 15 May 2017. It loses 20 seconds every hour. What time (in AM) will the clock show on 16 May 2017 at 4 AM?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 3:52.

GIVEN

• Correct at 4 AM on 15 May; loses 20 s per hour; read at 4 AM on 16 May.

SOLUTION

• Elapsed real time = 24 hours.

• Total loss = 20 s × 24 = 480 s = 8 minutes.

• Clock time = 4:00 AM − 8 min = 3:52 AM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Loss per day = 20 s × 24 = 480 s = 8 min. Subtract from 4:00 → 3:52.

NOTE

• A slow clock shows an EARLIER time (subtract the loss); a fast clock shows a later time (add the gain).

question: The present ages of A and B is 13 years and 16 years respectively. What will be the ratio of ages of A and B after 7 years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 20 : 23.

GIVEN

• Present ages: A = 13 years, B = 16 years.

SOLUTION

• After 7 years: A = 13 + 7 = 20; B = 16 + 7 = 23.

• Ratio = 20 : 23.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add 7 to each age and write the ratio: 20 : 23.

NOTE

• 'After n years' adds n to every person's age; 'n years ago' subtracts n. The ratio is then formed directly.

question: The ratio of the present age of a father to the present age of his son is 7 : 2. The product of their present ages in years is 350. 4 years ago from present, what was the ratio of ages of father and son respectively?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 31 : 6.

GIVEN

• Father : Son = 7 : 2; product of present ages = 350; find ratio 4 years ago.

SOLUTION

• Let father = 7x, son = 2x. Product = 7x × 2x = 14x² = 350 → x² = 25 → x = 5.

• Present: father = 35, son = 10.

• 4 years ago: father = 31, son = 6 → ratio = 31 : 6.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 14x² = 350 → x = 5 → ages 35 & 10; drop 4 each → 31 : 6.

NOTE

• Turn the given ratio into 7x : 2x, use the product/sum condition to find x, then adjust for the time shift.
